Only 10% of the total person trips are between the downtown area and the airport. Also, 15% of total person trips average a distance of 3 miles from the airport; 54% average 9 miles; 86% average 18 miles. Neither this distribution nor the projected volumes for the Airport Spur support an exclusive transitway.
There are approximately 2.15 inbound vehicles per enplaning passenger. Unless new transit concepts are developed, any change in occupancy rates depends almost entirely on improvements in bus service. Until specific plans are adopted for bus routes, no predictions can be made. The best chance for attracting more use of buses is increased time savings over their scheduled routes which the Airport Spur will provide.
11. The proposed Airport Spur will be in conformance with national policy of integrating ground and air transportation by directly connecting Milwaukee County's freeway system with Mitchell Field. The Airport Spur will also provide an opportunity for improved modified rapid bus transit to the area as an alternative to continued automobile use.
The proposed facility will be in conformance with SEWRPC's regional land use and transportation plans and will serve to implement the Milwaukee County Jurisdictional Highway System Plan, and Milwaukee Area Transit Plan. These plans are actively being used for the development of all transportation systems in Milwaukee County and the City of Milwaukee.
